message.content:
You are a READ-ONLY code reviewer. Do NOT modify any files. Review ONLY the change below for ONE angle: **Simplification** — unnecessary complexity the diff adds (redundant/derivable state, copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code, over-long comments). Name the simpler form that does the same job.

Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim. The change transports two Andes CSRs (mcache_ctl 0x7CA, mmisc_ctl 0x7D0) across the QEMU->vsim hybrid handoff, mirroring existing fcsr/mscratch/L24-trap-CSR transport.

Read these files (they're short) to judge in context:
- include/hybrid/state_abi.h (the new mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl fields + their ~10-line comment block)
- include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (new offset asserts)
- qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c (lines ~48-60 struct, ~233-238 resolve_handles, ~387-397 drain_state_into)
- verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp (constants ~56-64, restore ~229-245)
- verilator/tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp (new TEST_CASE ~589, compare to the L24 test ~545)
- verilator/tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp (the split test ~83)

Specific things to assess:
1. Comment volume: the new state_abi.h field comment (~10 lines), the resume_driver.hpp restore comment (~9 lines), plus comments at the plugin struct, resolve_handles, and drain_state_into all re-explain the same "caches resume disabled" rationale. Is the rationale repeated more times than necessary? Suggest which to trim to a one-liner + pointer, keeping ONE authoritative explanation. (Match the surrounding code's comment density — neighboring CSRs like fcsr/mscratch have their own comments, so some is idiomatic.)
2. Is the new state_abi.test.cpp split into two TEST_CASEs warranted, or could it be one?
3. Any redundant/derivable state or dead code introduced?

Return a short findings list: file, line, one-line summary, the simpler form. If it's already appropriately simple for this codebase's conventions, say so explicitly. Verify claims by reading the actual files.

attachment.content:
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	// Wire contract between the QEMU TCG plugin and vsim. Both sides write/read
2	// `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte through a shared file.
3	//
4	// Stability: never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add new
5	// fields by consuming bytes from `reserved`, or by introducing v2 alongside.
6	//
7	// Endianness: multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64
8	// host). The format is not endian-portable; cross-endian use would need an
9	// explicit byte-swap path.
10	//
11	// C and C++ both compile this header.
12	
13	#ifndef HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
14	#define HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
15	
16	#include <stdint.h>
17	#include <stddef.h>
18	
19	#ifdef __cplusplus
20	extern "C" {
21	#endif
22	
23	#define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
24	// Version 2 (L11): vreg[] widened from 64 to 128 bytes per register, which
25	// shifts every field after it. Readers reject version-1 files loudly (all
26	// three consumers check magic + version + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
27	#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 2u
28	
29	#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64 (1u << 0)
30	#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP   (1u << 1)
31	#define HYBRID_FLAG_V    (1u << 2)
32	
33	// VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
34	// VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
35	// span per vector register; the LIVE width is the runtime `vlenb` field
36	// below, so one struct layout serves every engine config and the legs
37	// never disagree on offsets. A producer whose vlenb exceeds this ceiling
38	// must refuse to drain (see hybrid_v_drain_policy) rather than truncate.
39	#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX 128
40	
41	// L26: bytes reserved for the V-register transport scratch page -- 32 vector
42	// registers at the wire-format span. The driver maps this many bytes ABOVE
43	// the program's --mem-size (so the scratch sits past the program's RAM), and
44	// vsim's v_scratch_gpa() / kVScratchBytes use the same count. Shared here so
45	// the producer (driver mmap sizing) and consumer (vsim sweep) never disagree.
46	#define HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
47	
48	// 64 PMP entries; pmpcfg slots reserved at 16 so the layout works for both
49	// RV64 (8 entries/CSR) and a future RV32 (4 entries/CSR) packing.
50	#define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
51	#define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
52	
53	// All fields are naturally 8-byte aligned, so __attribute__((packed)) is
54	// unnecessary and would force unaligned access codegen. Layout is locked by
55	// the static_asserts in state_abi_check.h.
56	struct hybrid_state_v1 {
57	  uint32_t magic;
58	  uint32_t version;
59	  uint32_t flags;
60	  uint32_t hart_id;
61	  uint64_t pc;
62	  uint64_t priv;  // 0=U, 1=S, 3=M
63	
64	  uint64_t gpr[32];
65	  uint64_t fpr[32];
66	
67	  uint64_t mstatus;
68	  uint64_t mepc;
69	  uint64_t mtvec;
70	  uint64_t mcause;
71	  uint64_t mtval;
72	  uint64_t mscratch;
73	  uint64_t medeleg;
74	  uint64_t mideleg;
75	  uint64_t mip;
76	  uint64_t mie;
77	  uint64_t mcycle;
78	  uint64_t minstret;
79	  uint64_t satp;
80	
81	  uint64_t pmpcfg[HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM];
82	  uint64_t pmpaddr[HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM];
83	
84	  uint64_t vstart;
85	  uint64_t vtype;
86	  uint64_t vl;
87	  uint64_t vlenb;
88	  uint8_t  vreg[32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX];
89	  uint64_t vxsat;
90	  uint64_t vxrm;
91	  uint64_t vcsr;
92	
93	  // F13: warmup-window snapshot of cycle/instret counters, captured K insns
94	  // after vsim entry. Drain-only metadata; ResumeDriver never restores them.
95	  // Both zero when --vsim-warmup-icount=0 or the workload exited inside the
96	  // warmup window. Consumes 16 bytes from the original 232-byte reserved tail.
97	  uint64_t mcycle_at_measure_start;
98	  uint64_t minstret_at_measure_start;
99	
100	  // L20: FP control/status -- frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], live when
101	  // HYBRID_FLAG_FP is set. Drained by the plugin, restored by ResumeDriver,
102	  // re-read by StateDrain. Pre-L20 state files carry 0 here (reserved bytes
103	  // are written as zero), which reads back as the reset value (RNE, no
104	  // flags) -- exactly the old behavior, so no version bump.
105	  uint64_t fcsr;
106	
107	  // Andes machine setup CSRs that crt0 writes once at boot and the program
108	  // then runs under: mcache_ctl (0x7CA) enables the L1 I/D caches, mmisc_ctl
109	  // (0x7D0) holds misc machine config. Drained by the plugin, restored by
110	  // ResumeDriver. Without these the cycle engine resumes at the ROI with
111	  // caches DISABLED (its reset default) because the enabling write happened
112	  // on the functional engine, which has no cache model -- inflating the
113	  // measured window severalfold. Old state files carry 0 here (reserved
114	  // bytes read back as zero), i.e. "leave at the hart's reset value", which
115	  // is the pre-existing behavior, so no version bump. Restored tolerantly:
116	  // an engine without these custom CSRs mirrors the write as a no-op.
117	  uint64_t mcache_ctl;
118	  uint64_t mmisc_ctl;
119	
120	  uint8_t  reserved[192];  // zero-initialise on write; 256 - 3*8 (vxsat/vxrm/vcsr) - 2*8 (warmup) - 8 (fcsr) - 2*8 (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl)
121	};
122	
123	#ifdef __cplusplus
124	}  // extern "C"
125	#endif
126	
127	#include "hybrid/state_abi_check.h"
128	
129	#endif  // HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
130

content.text:
## Simplification review: mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl transport

Verified against the working-tree diff (uncommitted) plus the sibling `fcsr`/`mscratch`/L24 transport for calibration. The change is small and closely mirrors the existing pattern. One real redundancy, the rest is appropriately simple.

### Finding 1 - the full rationale paragraph is duplicated at full length (the one real issue)

The "why" paragraph -- *cycle engine resumes with caches DISABLED because the enabling write happened on the cache-less functional engine -> inflates the measured window severalfold* -- appears at near-verbatim full length in **two** places:

- `include/hybrid/state_abi.h:107-116` (~10 lines)
- `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp:232-239` (~8 lines)

Plus two short restatements in the plugin (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:51-53` and `:390-391`).

This is *more* than the codebase convention. The cited siblings keep the full rationale in exactly **one** authoritative spot:
- `fcsr`: ~5-line rationale at `state_abi.h:100-105`; the resume site (`resume_driver.hpp:137-138`) is a 2-line note.
- L24 trap CSRs: the full rationale lives only at the resume site (`resume_driver.hpp:219-225`); the ABI struct just lists the fields.

Simpler form: keep **one** full explanation. The duplicated span is only the middle mechanism sentences ("resumes ... caches DISABLED ... inflating ... severalfold"). Recommend keeping the full version at `resume_driver.hpp` (the fix site, matching where L24's rationale lives) and trimming `state_abi.h:107-116` down to the wire-format-relevant facts it uniquely carries -- what the two CSRs are, "drained by plugin / restored by ResumeDriver," and the "old files carry 0 = reset value, no version bump" note (this mirrors fcsr's ABI comment and is *not* in the resume_driver copy). That drops ~5 lines and leaves it at fcsr-comment length, with a one-line pointer for the "why."

The two plugin comments (3 + 2 lines) are at idiomatic density (match `mscratch`/neighbors), so leave them; at most the drain-site one at `:390-391` repeats the struct-decl facts verbatim and could become a one-line "see hybrid_state_v1" -- lowest priority.

### Finding 2 - state_abi.test.cpp split into two TEST_CASEs: warranted, not a finding

The split was forced and correct. The old `L20: fcsr ... before reserved` test asserted `reserved == fcsr + 8`, which the new fields make false, so that assertion *had* to move. Re-homing "before reserved" onto `mmisc_ctl` in a separate TEST_CASE matches the file's one-group-per-case convention (separate L20, F13, etc.). Collapsing back to one case would be against the file's grain. Appropriately simple as-is.

### Finding 3 - redundant/derivable state and dead code

- No derivable/redundant state: `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl` are genuinely new transported values, not computable from other fields.
- Not dead code: the restore has a real runtime effect (caches on before measurement).
- Restore-only is fine: I confirmed `state_drain.hpp` is untouched, so these CSRs are drained + restored but never re-read at drain / compared at `--verify`. That matches the accepted `mtvec` precedent (restored, not re-drained, per CLAUDE.md). Consistent, not a defect.

### Secondary - copy-paste test body (consistent with the file, optional)

`resume_driver.test.cpp:589-627` is a ~38-line near-clone of the L24 case at `:545-587`; only the test name, the state setup, and the `want[]` contents differ -- the entire scan-for-write-COMMAND-then-check-DATA0/DATA1 loop is identical. This is the third copy of that loop in the file (mscratch and L24 already have it).

Simpler form: a shared helper, e.g. `assert_csr_write_cmds(bus, {{0x7CA, s.mcache_ctl}, {0x7D0, s.mmisc_ctl}})`, would collapse each body to setup + one call. Caveat: the duplication is the file's established idiom, so the clean fix is a single helper applied to *all three* call sites, not just this addition -- a broader refactor, not something to block this diff on. Per "don't duplicate code," worth doing as a follow-up tidy across the file rather than adding a fourth bespoke copy later.

### Bottom line
Only Finding 1 is worth acting on now: collapse the doubled full-length rationale to one authoritative copy (~5 lines saved). Everything else is appropriately simple for this codebase's conventions.
